Six visualizations

Each one turns a sentence the app prints today into a shape. Pick the ones you want; nothing here is wired into the app yet.

◔1 · Week burn-up WEEK · REPLACES PACE TEXT

Answers: "am I behind, and by how much?" The gold line is what you've worked, the dashed line is the 8h-per-workday plan, and the orange area is the gap. The two dotted lines show where you finish at your pace and the pace you'd need.

◔1b · Month burn-up MONTH · BESIDE THE CALENDAR

Same chart, month scale. The plan line steps flat on weekends, so days off read correctly without a legend.

▭2 · Day ribbon POPOVER · UNDER TODAY
4h 30m₹6,750
Solid = work · orange = paused · dashed = forecast to 5:30 PM

The whole day in 20 points of height. It replaces nothing; it sits under the Today figures so one look shows the day's shape, the gaps, and where it ends.

⋯4a · Your rhythm ANALYTICS · SPRINT PATTERNS

When do you actually start and stop? One line per workday, from clock-in (gold) to clock-out (ink). Averages: in around 9:21 AM, out around 6:25 PM.

▥4b · Sprint lengths ANALYTICS · SPRINT PATTERNS
129sprints in October
1.5–2hmost common length

Pairs with the eye-break reminder. If most sprints run past 2h, a 45-minute reminder is the one that will actually fire.

₹5 · Cumulative earnings ANALYTICS · BESIDE TOTALS
₹12,750November so far
₹74,550October by the same day

Answers "how much this month compared with last?" with the previous period as a ghost line, cut to the same day like the Totals card.

◌6 · Menu bar progress ring MENU BAR · STATUS PILL
Today 00:30:11 With the ring 00:30:11 00:12:40

Daily goal progress without opening the popover. The ring is drawn in the pill's text colour, so it works in every theme. It changes once a minute, so it adds no cost while you work.

3D art: the three scopes

The same SceneKit renders placed three ways. Moments only keeps every figure untouched; the third column shows what "playful everywhere" costs a ledger.

The rendered set and theme tinting

Rendered by scripts/render-3d-assets.swift (SceneKit, headless, Apple frameworks only). Pass an accent hex and every object re-tints to the theme, so all 24 palettes get their own set at build time with no runtime 3D.
